findings.issue_text: The repo-search memo key flattens strong and weak subject tokens into one space-joined string, so two findings with the same normalized own file and the same token union but different strong/weak partitions collide on one memo entry; the shared entry applies EvidenceFor's admission bar (1 strong or 2 weak hits) from whichever finding searched first. Constructing such a collision requires two texts whose sorted token sequence is identical while camel/underscore placement differs per token under the same own file — not reachable by any realistic finding pair — and even then the mis-shared evidence is only offered to the judge for weighing, never deciding. Non-blocking; noted for a future key that joins strong and weak lists separately.

evidence.note: All callers of the changed ContextForGapClaim signature (kind.go:688, kind.go:819, gapclaim_test.go) pass the new repo parameter; no stale call sites remain.
Grep pattern tokens derive from ident/bareFile regexes (word chars, dot, dash only) - no ERE metacharacters can corrupt the git grep -E alternation.
Budget arithmetic: primary share + path shares + body shares sum exactly to the caller budget; reserved-but-unused shares only under-spend, never overflow.

Failure semantics verified end to end: seam errors are memoized, counted (repo_search_errors rollup, repo-error matrix row), and never rendered as evidence of absence; gapClaimRepoNone is emitted only for a completed empty search.
ShowSeam distinguishes ls-tree absence from command failure, preserving the bias-toward-confirmation guard the new ShowHead contract documents.
No .beads or metaswarm directory in the repository root; rubric advisory-mode condition for PASS_ADVISORY is met with in-diff test evidence present.
